title: Sound design with it
description: From a preset to your own sound: the circuit, locks, evolving from a patch, the node bank, modulation chains, the commit duel, and the lineage.

lines.text: Start from a preset, and end with a sound of your own.
Open the circuit in PATCH. Every edit is live under your fingers.
Knobs read in musical units, like hertz, milliseconds and decibels.
Above the rack, the model's guess for this patch updates as you edit.
Find what you love and lock it, a knob by its dot or a module by its square.
Or lock every knob, or all the wiring, in one press.
Then press Evolve from this.
The search changes only what you left unlocked, and puts one new patch on the bench.
To change the structure, click a module in the node bank.
It is in your hand, and every socket it fits lights up.
Green inserts it after what is there. Amber replaces it.
Rest on a socket and press play to hear it spliced in, before you place it.
Its card says what the module does and what it arrives set to.
It also says what the model believes about it, or that it does not know yet.
And it says what the model cannot hear. There is no stereo width in what it measures.
So it will never learn that you love a chorus for its width.
Modulation can chain.
In Ask The Dice, a sample and hold feeds a quantizer, and then a slew.
Together they play the oscillator's pitch as a random melody, in key and gliding.
Drop a shaper on a slot that is already modulated, and it wraps what is there.
Commit, and it asks which is better, the original or your edit, in random order.
Either answer teaches it.
If you already know, tick my edit is better and skip the comparison.
That answer is filed as a claim, and scored apart from heard ones.
Every change is one undo step.
Anything you unplug, delete or bypass waits in the held tray, even across a reload.
And the lineage in EVOLVE keeps the history of your edits and evolution's steps.
Each entry says what changed, and how far the model's estimate moved.
Lock what you know, evolve the rest, and keep what sounds like you.
